notes:
Deal background: enterprise analytics platform serving personalized recommendations and real-time reranking for ad partners. PoC started 2024-11. Heavy throughput (3000-5000 qps peak) with sub-60ms tail latency targets for reranking. Team of infra + ML engineers (internal MLOps).

Timeline (short):
- 2024-11-04: Inbound from engineering blog; initial qualification by Maya. Interested in Redwood for predictable latency and cost.
- 2024-11-12: Discovery call (AE + SE) — detailed Qs on KV cache, batching, token costs. Fireflies: ff_1287cobalt_call_20241203.
- 2024-11-25: Demo w/ Redwood Console (latency dashboards) — positive reaction to route fallback features. Follow-up: pricing deck shared (drive:/deals/cobalt-delta/pricing-deck-v2.pdf).
- 2024-12-10: Security RFP provided; requested SOC2/ISO artifacts. Ran internal cost model vs self-hosting; initial results showed self-hosting with quantized models still ~35% cheaper for sustained loads.
- 2024-12-18: Security review call — highlighted need for KMS + strict audit logs + residency. SOC2 gaps noted (drive:/security-reviews/cobalt-delta/soc2-gap-analysis.xlsx).
- 2025-01-06: Procurement paused due to company-wide budget freeze. Internal champion (Head of ML, Raj Patel) left 2025-01-22 — momentum dropped.
- 2025-02-05: Final touchpoint; customer confirmed they will pursue self-host route (vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM stack) to retain full control of keys, custom kernels, and long-term cost. Closed-lost.

Key quotes / signals:
- "We need end-to-end control over key material and kernel selection for latency — it's non-negotiable."
- "Even with Redwood's autoscaling, our long tail token costs don't line up with the 24/7 traffic profile."

Primary reasons lost:
- Cost over 12–24 month horizon favored self-hosting (esp. committed hardware + TensorRT inference).
- Security/compliance comfort: preferred owning KMS/HSM and audit trail in-house.
- Org changes: internal champion left and procurement froze for Q1.

Technical notes captured by SE:
- Required support for TensorRT-LLM and Triton integrations; strong interest in quantized fp16/INT8 paths.
- KV cache persistence and long-context batch shaping are must-haves.
- On-prem pack + private control plane would have helped but licensing + timeline mismatch.

- Schedule 6mo win-back: reach out with new private packaging and hybrid cost scenarios.
